E1.title: House of Balloons
E1.text: The title House of Balloons originates from a house, located at 65 Spencer Avenue, Parkdale, Toronto, in which the Weeknd and his friends used to live.

E2.title: House of Balloons
E2.text: He said he and his friends would throw parties and added balloons for a more celebratory feel.

E3.title: House of Balloons
E3.text: The cover art depicts a woman with her face obscured by balloons and her left breast exposed.

E4.title: House of Balloons
E4.text: The Weeknd asked his friend La Mar Taylor for a cover photograph because the mixtape was ready for release.

E5.title: House of Balloons
E5.text: Taylor photographed the cover at his house with his ex-girlfriend.

E7.title: House of Balloons
E7.text: House of Balloons is the debut mixtape by the Canadian singer-songwriter the Weeknd.

E8.title: House of Balloons
E8.text: It was self-released free of charge on March 21, 2011, through his own record label, XO.

E9.title: House of Balloons
E9.text: House of Balloons was commercially reissued in 2012 through Republic Records as the first disc of the Weeknd's compilation album Trilogy, and was reissued in its original version with all samples present in 2021.

E10.title: The Weeknd
E10.text: House of Balloons has received substantial retrospective recognition.

E11.title: The Weeknd
E11.text: It appeared on decade-end album lists by Pitchfork, Vice and Slant Magazine, and in 2025, Rolling Stone included it in its list of the 250 greatest albums of the 21st century so far; the magazine's entry described the mixtape as the standout in Tesfaye's catalogue despite his subsequent commercial success.

E12.title: House of Balloons
E12.text: from the anime Fate/stay night, and is supported with a sound of wind and a mini-motif.

E13.title: House of Balloons
E13.text: Throughout the song, the Weeknd murmurs for his partner's sympathy as he admits his regret and reaffirms his loyalty to his partner, on whom he cheated the night before.

E14.title: House of Balloons
E14.text: House of Balloons is categorized as an alternative R&B record that incorporates elements of other genres, such as dream pop, electro, rock, hip-hop, trip hop, lo-fi, pop, and gothic rock.

E15.title: House of Balloons
E15.text: The Weeknd's mixing of genres with samples reflects a movement of black pop/R&B artists interacting with music from white, indie, pop, and rock artists.

E16.title: House of Balloons
E16.text: Symbolizing his experiences in Toronto, House of Balloons explores but does not romanticize the loneliness of partying at night, detailing late-night sexual and drug escapades, the aftermath of partying, and hedonistic fantasies.

E17.title: House of Balloons
E17.text: After releasing music under aliases in 2009, the Weeknd met with several producers, including Cirkut, Illangelo, and Jeremy Rose in 2010 and 2011 in Toronto, where songs on the mixtape were created.

E18.title: House of Balloons
E18.text: In January 2011, Doc McKinney and Illangelo became the project's primary producers.

E19.title: House of Balloons
E19.text: House of Balloons is an alternative R&B record that incorporates elements of dream pop, electro, rock, pop, and other genres.

E20.title: House of Balloons
E20.text: The lyrics symbolize the Weeknd's experiences in Toronto, and describe drug abuse, sexual encounters, and parties.

E21.title: House of Balloons
E21.text: House of Balloons received widespread acclaim; music critics praised its dark aesthetic, production, and lyrical content.

E22.title: House of Balloons
E22.text: House of Balloons was shortlisted for the 2011 Polaris Music Prize, and it was frequently listed as one of the best projects of 2011.

E23.title: House of Balloons
E23.text: The Weeknd's anonymity during the project's rollout is attributed to fueling his popularity growth, inspiring artists to use the same approach.

E24.title: House of Balloons
E24.text: House of Balloons is also cited as altering the R&B genre, with its darker production, lyricism, and vocals contrasting with the more-upbeat tone of late-2000s-decade R&B.

E25.title: House of Balloons
E25.text: mastered-and-mixed version of House of Balloons, including "Twenty Eight", was released as an LP record on August 14, 2015.

E26.title: House of Balloons
E26.text: On its tenth anniversary, the Weeknd cleared all of the samples on House of Balloons and releasing its original 2011 version to streaming services on March 21, 2021.

E27.title: House of Balloons
E27.text: American artist Daniel Arsham was engaged to create merchandise for the anniversary and special artwork for a limited-edition LP record.

E28.title: House of Balloons
E28.text: Release dates and formats for House of Balloons

E29.title: House of Balloons
E29.text: Region | Date | Label(s) | Format(s) | Edition | Ref.

E30.title: House of Balloons
E30.text: Various | March 21, 2011 | XO | Digital downloadstreaming | 9-track free of charge |

E33.title: House of Balloons
E33.text: Some critics, despite their positive reviews, also criticized House of Balloons; these reviews include those from Ewing, Andrew Baer of No Ripcord, and Will Hermes of Rolling Stone.

E34.title: House of Balloons
E34.text: Ewing believed that the Weeknd's vocals and lyrics were not strong by "R&B standards", Baer believed its sound to not be innovative, while Hermes thought the mixtape could have spawned hit songs if the Weeknd improved lyrically and sonically.

E35.title: House of Balloons
E35.text: Dom Sinacola of Cokemachineglow said the project "lack[ed] dynamism".

E36.title: House of Balloons
E36.text: House of Balloons was met with widespread critical acclaim.

E37.title: House of Balloons
E37.text: At Metacritic, which assigns a normalized rating out of 100 to reviews from professional publications, House of Balloons received an average score of 87, based on 16 reviews.

E38.title: House of Balloons
E38.text: The aggregator AnyDecentMusic? gave it 8.0 out of 10, based on its assessment of the critical consensus.

E39.title: House of Balloons
E39.text: Based on these statistics, Metacritic determined House of Balloons is the third-best-reviewed project of 2011, while AnyDecentMusic? determined it is the 10th-best-reviewed project of the year.
